expectations.text: Recognizes that no capability breakdown was provided
expectations.evidence: Title is 'Before I design the architecture, I need the capability breakdown'. Line 3: 'Right now I have neither the breakdown nor a description of the app ("my app" is unspecified)'.

expectations.text: Tries to retrieve the breakdown via the librarian skill, or asks the user to provide it
expectations.evidence: Does both. Section 2: 'Normally I'd try to pull a saved breakdown via the librarian skill before asking you. The librarian skill is not available in this run' and provides the exact librarian commands (python scripts/librarian.py search/list, category specs, scope project). Section 1 also asks the user to paste it or give a file path.

expectations.text: Does NOT fabricate a full architecture for an unspecified app without any capability basis
expectations.evidence: No stack, components, or architecture were produced. Footer line 42: 'No architecture was generated because the app and its capabilities are unspecified — designing one now would invent your product rather than architect it.'

expectations.text: Asks a small number of targeted questions (not an exhaustive questionnaire)
expectations.evidence: Section 3 asks exactly four constraint questions and frames them as 'the only constraints that actually change my recommendation', explicitly avoiding an exhaustive questionnaire.

expectations.text: If it asks constraint questions, they focus on high-leverage items (scale, team, hosting, compliance)
expectations.evidence: The four questions are: 1. Scale & load, 2. Team (skills/size), 3. Hosting (cloud/on-prem/existing infra), 4. Hard constraints (budget, compliance: HIPAA/PCI/GDPR/SOC 2, must-use/avoid tech). Maps directly to scale, team, hosting, compliance.

expectations.text: Suggests running the solution-architect skill first if no breakdown exists
expectations.evidence: Line 10: 'If no — I'd recommend running the solution-architect skill first to produce one; it makes for a much stronger, fully-traceable architecture.'

expectations.text: Does NOT attempt to persist/save output
expectations.evidence: No save/persist action taken. It only describes a future intent to 'hand it to the librarian skill to persist' once it actually produces an architecture; nothing was written this turn.

expectations.text: Behavior reflects 'build on the breakdown' principle rather than guessing the whole system
expectations.evidence: Line 3: 'I decide the how ... by building on a capability breakdown that says what the app does ... a fabricated stack would be unanchored guesswork.' It explicitly defers to the breakdown rather than guessing the system, and cites the skill's Step 0.

claims.claim: The librarian skill is not available in this run
claims.evidence: Consistent with the harness sandbox not exposing the librarian skill; the response correctly degrades to providing the commands an agent with access could run rather than claiming to have retrieved anything.

claims.claim: Designing a stack now would mean inventing the product
claims.evidence: Justified — the prompt gives no app description or capabilities, so any stack would be unanchored. The response correctly refuses to fabricate.

workarounds: Librarian skill unavailable; provided manual librarian commands and asked the user to paste the breakdown instead

suggestions.assertion: Tries to retrieve the breakdown via the librarian skill, or asks the user to provide it
suggestions.reason: The OR makes this easy to pass on the 'asks the user' branch alone. Since the librarian-retrieval behavior is the skill-specific differentiator, consider a separate assertion that specifically credits referencing/invoking the librarian skill, so the librarian behavior is measured distinctly from generic 'ask the user'.

suggestions.assertion: Does NOT attempt to persist/save output
suggestions.reason: Trivially satisfied here because there was no output to persist. It only meaningfully discriminates in evals where an architecture IS produced; for the ask-first eval it is near-vacuous.

eval_feedback.overall: Assertions are well-targeted for this under-specification scenario and clearly separate skill from baseline. Two assertions (the OR-joined librarian one and the no-persist one) are easy to pass for the wrong reasons; splitting/sharpening them would increase discrimination.
